hook: The Marathon finally *listened* to the Bronx
dek: Sunday marks 50 years of the five-borough course, and its first route change in 15 years came from Mott Haven.

slides.label: The weekend
slides.text: Saturday night the city puts on a costume. Sunday, Nov. 1, it runs the *TCS New York City Marathon*, marking *50 years* since the race left Central Park for all five boroughs.

slides.label: The old loop
slides.text: Between miles 20 and 21, runners came off the Willis Avenue Bridge into Mott Haven and looped a block on *East 140th Street*, home to a Western Beef and a *24-hour laundromat*.

slides.label: The neighbors
slides.text: Across Morris Avenue sit the *Patterson Houses*, nearly *1,800 units* of public housing. Residents said the old route cut them off from the supermarket and other local businesses.

slides.label: The new route
slides.text: For the first time in *15 years*, the course changes. Runners stay on Alexander Avenue, then take East 141st Street, Third Avenue and East 138th Street. *Seven turns become five*.

slides.label: Still closed
slides.text: It is still not a normal Bronx Sunday. Street sections close *7am to 8:30pm*, and the Willis and Madison Avenue bridges close *7:30am to 6:30pm*. Plan the grocery run for Saturday.

slides.label: Fifty years
slides.text: The first five-borough race in 1976 had *2,090* participants. Last year *59,226* finished, a world record. More than *240,000* applied to this year's general drawing, also a record.

slides.label: Saturday first
slides.text: The *53rd Village Halloween Parade* steps off Saturday at 7pm from Canal Street, theme *Body & Soul*. Marching is free in costume; line up at Canal and Sixth, 6:30pm to 9pm.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: NYRR called it *minor adjustments*. In the Bronx it reads as civic power: a public housing community asked for *two fewer turns*, and got them. Go cheer uptown at mile 20.

caption_instagram:
The NYC Marathon turns 50 on Sunday, and the biggest change this year came from one South Bronx block.

For years, runners between miles 20 and 21 looped around East 140th Street in Mott Haven, past a Western Beef and a 24-hour laundromat. Residents of the Patterson Houses, nearly 1,800 units of public housing, said the old route cut them off from the supermarket and other local businesses. Now, for the first time in 15 years, the course changes: runners stay on Alexander Avenue, then take East 141st Street, Third Avenue and East 138th Street to the Madison Avenue Bridge. Seven turns become five. More than 50,000 runners are expected, after a world-record 59,226 finishers last year. Before all that, the 53rd Village Halloween Parade steps off Saturday at 7pm from Canal Street.

The other side: New York Road Runners calls the changes minor adjustments, and sections of Bronx streets still close from 7am to 8:30pm Sunday.

caption_linkedin:
The world's largest marathon just showed what community input looks like in practice.

For its 50th five-borough year, the TCS New York City Marathon changed its course for the first time in 15 years. Residents of the Patterson Houses, a Mott Haven public housing development of nearly 1,800 units, said the old route cut them off from a supermarket and local businesses. New York Road Runners adjusted the Bronx stretch, cutting seven turns to five, and said the race "wouldn't be what it is without the support of the communities the course runs through."

The scale is real: 59,226 finishers last year, more than 240,000 applications for this year's general drawing, and a charity program with more than 670 partners aiming for more than $100 million. For any large event operator, the lesson is that small accommodations for neighbors carry outsized goodwill.

How should big city events weigh spectacle against the blocks they run through?

By The Innovators Den. Sources: Time Out New York, amNY, Endurance.biz, 6sqft.

title: The NYC Marathon Turns 50 and Finally Listens to the South Bronx
